claims.text: \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has the Schur basis indexed by partitions in the \(r\times(n-r)\) box. [source-2@L1318-L1324|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1318: The $\ZZ$-basis for $\Lambda$ given by the Schur functions $s_\lambda$ 
1319: has the property that the $\ZZ$-submodule $I_{r,n-r}$ spanned by all $s_\lambda$
1320: with  $\lambda \not\subseteq (n-r)^r$ forms an ideal, and the
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism
1322: $$
1323: \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} \quad \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \quad \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}/\ZZ[\xx]^W_+ \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J} 
1324:                      \quad \left( \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ) \right)

claims.text: Conditional on the stipulated box/Schur/Pieri presentation, \(i,j\ge2\), \(q=i+p\), \(r=j+c\), and \(\min(p,c)=1\), the degree enumeration is \[ J_d=\mathbb Zx_0,\quad J_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\{x_1,y_1\},\quad J_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\{\gamma,x_2,z,y_2,\theta\}, \] omitting \(\gamma\) for \(p=1\) and \(\theta\) for \(c=1\). Moreover \[ A_1=\langle h_1\rangle,\quad A_2=\langle h_2,h_1^2\rangle,\quad A_3=\langle h_3,h_2h_1,h_1^3\rangle, \] and, writing \(r_2=h_2x_1,r_3=h_2y_1,r_4=h_1\gamma,r_5=h_1x_2,r_6=h_1z,r_7=h_1y_2,r_8=h_1\theta\), \[ h_2h_1x_0=r_2+r_3,\quad h_1^3x_0=r_4+r_5+2r_6+r_7+r_8, \] \[ h_1^2x_1=r_4+r_5+r_6,\qquad h_1^2y_1=r_6+r_7+r_8. \]
